messages:
Alex Li: :rotating_light: Pager - getting alerted for high 5xx rate and TLS handshake failures to api.redwood-inference.com across multiple regions. Errors started ~03:45 UTC. Cloudflare edge responses showing 523/525 and some TCP handshake timeouts. Impact metric spike: 18% requests failing on prod-prod cluster.
Incident Bot: PagerDuty triggered the on-call team (Alex Li). Incident ticket ID PD-17900 created.
Alex Li: I'm on it. @Maya can you pull tls logs and cf logs? Brian, can you check LB health and origins?
Maya Rao: looking at the edge logs now. Correlating: Cloudflare return codes show TLS handshake aborted by client (alert: 40) and some handshake failure at Cloudflare->origin. Seen in us-east-1, eu-west-1.
Brian Chen: origin health is fine, backends answering 200 for direct checks. Running a direct curl to origin works. Suspicious it's an edge-level issue between CF and clients or CF->origin TLS negotiation.
Olivia Park: customer impact: a subset of tokenized API calls (high QPS customers) report timeouts. CS has 3 active tickets calling in. I'll update status page if we confirm degradation.
Alex Li: confirm reproduction:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health -o /dev/null -s -w "%{http_code}\n"
# sample output shows TLS handshake failures intermittently and some 524s
```
Maya Rao: I pulled Cloudflare diagnostics, there's an ongoing anomaly in their edge POPs causing TLS renegotiation and handshake jitter. CF status shows intermittent issues in some POPs but not full outage: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/xxxxx (internal link)
Brian Chen: short mitigation plan proposals: 1) shift traffic away from affected CF pops via Cloudflare Traffic Steering (requires CF support), 2) switch DNS to bypass CF (point to internal LB) temporarily, 3) enable origin passthrough route for critical customer routes. Each has tradeoffs.
Alex Li: quick decision: do option 2 for a quick mitigation for critical customers — update DNS for api-critical.redwood.com to point to lb-direct.redwood.net with very low TTL, so only subset of customers are rerouted. We'll keep main api on CF to avoid cache/edge issues for everything else.
Maya Rao: prepping DNS change. Brian, can you confirm origin TLS cert is valid for direct host (lb-direct.redwood.net) and that ALPN/protocols match clients?
Brian Chen: cert ok, TLS 1.2+1.3 enabled. I'll post the check:
```text
openssl s_client -connect lb-direct.redwood.net:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com
# VERIFY return code: 0 (ok)
```
Maya Rao: updating Route53 record for api-critical.redwood.com -> lb-direct.redwood.net. Using low TTL 30s. Making change now.
Incident Bot: DNS change detected by infra-deploy-bot. Change ID: dns-1790012345-1.
Alex Li: monitoring. Rolling update to routing policy: target 5% of traffic -> api-critical host first, will increase if success.
Olivia Park: alerting top 20 customers on the phone (CS taking notes). We'll update status page to "degraded" with note: some TLS handshakes failing due to third-party CDN (Cloudflare) issues, partial failover in progress.
Maya Rao: after DNS change, error rate for the critical prefix dropped from 22% -> 4% in the rerouted pool within 2 mins. Latency stable.
Brian Chen: confirming logs show direct-origin responses are good. No obvious errors.
Alex Li: escalation to Cloudflare: we've opened a support ticket and asked for POP-level mitigation/traffic steering. CF says they're applying a mitigation and digging into edge TLS infra. Reference CF ticket CF-98127.
Maya Rao: rolling additional 20% traffic to direct host (total ~25%). Observability dashboards updated. No regressions.
Olivia Park: customers notified, one enterprise asked for a dedicated bypass — noted as action item.
Brian Chen: small follow-up: temporarily disabled HTTP/2 at edge for the rerouted host to avoid a rare HPACK/connection reuse bug we saw historically. Change done.
Alex Li: on-call handoff in 2 hours to Maya. I'll stay until we have CF confirmation and traffic is stable at <1% error.
Maya Rao: acknowledged, will take over post-handoff.
PagerDuty: Acknowledged incident PD-17900. Next on-call: Maya Rao at 05:45 UTC.
Olivia Park: impact summary for now: ~12-18% of total requests across regions affected at peak, primarily auth/token routes for a small customer subset. Mitigation: partial DNS bypass for critical customers reduced error rate to ~4%.
Alex Li: severity set to SEV2 — partial widespread degradation with active mitigation. Postmortem: required to cover root cause (third-party edge TLS), why automatic fallback didn't trigger for some routes, and runbook updates.
Maya Rao: action items captured:
- Runbook: add explicit DNS bypass steps and pre-authorized LB hostnames (owner: Brian)
- Observability: add edge-pop-level TLS handshake alert (owner: Maya)
- CS/Support: template for customer communications (owner: Olivia)
- Enterprise follow-up: offer temporary dedicated bypass and timeline from CF (owner: Alex)
Alex Li: good work. I'll update PD ticket and status page. Leaving notes for handoff.
Maya Rao: taking over monitoring. If CF confirms fix, we will phase traffic back to Cloudflare with canary steps.
Olivia Park: I'll prepare the customer-facing post (short note + ETA TBD).
Alex Li: signing off from on-call in 10 mins. Handoff complete. :thumbsup:
Incident Bot: Incident PD-17900 status updated to "mitigated - partial bypass in place".
Alex Li: Postmortem requested. Expected due date in 7 days.
Olivia Park: adding impacted tickets to the incident for follow-up credits/rca notes.
Maya Rao: monitoring continues. Closing thread for real-time coordination, will reopen if new regressions occur.
